headline: GOLD SURGES $170 ON ADP MISS — 38K Private Jobs Vs 47K Expected Cuts September Hike Odds; Friday NFP Is Make-Or-Break For $4,400 Recovery
snippet: Gold staged its sharpest single-session advance in months on September 2, recovering toward $4,360 after August ADP private payrolls came in at just 38,000 — nearly 10,000 below the 47,000 consensus — trimming September FOMC rate-hike odds from 70% back toward 66% and removing a key inflation amplifier as Strait of Hormuz tensions paused. The ADP miss follows soft July data and signals that the US labour market may finally be cracking under sustained high rates; if Friday's official Non-farm Payrolls report confirms the trend, the September hike thesis collapses and the gold bull case resets above $4,400. For precious metals investors, the ADP / NFP sequence this week is the most consequential data window since the January record high — a strong payrolls print Friday reinforces the hike, while a miss could drive a 3–5% single-session move in gold.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING DRILLS 38m AT 15.46 g/t AuEq — Apollo Breccia Extension Pushes System 170m Deeper And 100m North At Guayabales, Colombia
snippet: Collective Mining Ltd. (TSX: CNL) reported September 2 that a directional drill hole at the Apollo Breccia system in Caldas, Colombia returned 141.40 metres at 4.88 g/t gold equivalent from 170.10 metres depth, including 38.00 metres at 15.46 g/t AuEq — extending Apollo 170 vertical metres below any previous drilling on the northern flank and 100 metres laterally to the north. Geologists logged 31 instances of visible gold; the system remains open to the east, west, and at depth. Apollo is already one of the highest-grade bulk-tonnage breccia discoveries made by a junior in the Americas this decade; today's extension materially expands the resource envelope going into a resource update expected later this year as part of a 100,000-metre 2026 drill program.

headline: AUSTRALIAN GOLD & COPPER 'MAJOR DISCOVERY' AT EVERGREEN: 17m @ 5.3 g/t AU, 163 g/t AG, 17.3% Pb+Zn — Second Bonanza Multi-Metal Find In Two Years At South Cobar, NSW
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper Ltd (ASX: AGC) reported September 2 that drill hole 26DDBR017 at its Evergreen prospect returned 17 metres at 5.3 g/t gold, 163 g/t silver, 0.8% copper, and 17.3% lead plus zinc from 128 metres depth — including an 8-metre high-grade core at 10.4 g/t Au, 311 g/t Ag, 1.2% Cu, and 29% Pb+Zn. The company describes Evergreen as its second significant gold-silver-base metals discovery within two years at South Cobar in New South Wales. Ten RC holes have been completed with a rig currently testing along strike; the polymetallic profile — bonanza gold and silver alongside commercial-grade copper, lead, and zinc — is unusual and raises the prospect of multiple processing revenue streams. At current gold and silver prices, the economics of a shallow multi-metal oxide-sulphide system in New South Wales are compelling.

headline: CASCADIA MINERALS NEARLY DOUBLES CARMACKS ZONE 2000S — Step-Out Holes Open 600m Corridor Toward Zone 147 At Road-Accessible Yukon Copper-Gold Project
snippet: Cascadia Minerals Ltd. (TSX-V: CAM) released September 1 results from five additional drill holes at its road-accessible Carmacks copper-gold project in central Yukon, demonstrating that Zone 2000S extends continuously for 300 metres toward the adjacent Zone 147 — nearly doubling documented strike length and opening a 600-metre mineralized corridor. The 2026 program has been expanded from 15,000 to 18,000 metres after consistently exceeding grade expectations, with earlier releases returning up to 82.69 metres at 1.12% copper and 0.64 g/t gold (1.78% CuEq). Carmacks sits 35 km from the past-producing Minto copper mine and is accessible year-round by government road — a logistical advantage that reduces capital costs and timeline risk relative to remote Yukon copper projects. At copper above $6.50/lb, the economic threshold for bulk-tonnage copper-gold in this jurisdiction is achievable at significantly lower grades than current results.

headline: ENERGY FUELS GOES ALL-IN ON RARE EARTHS — $725M US Government Support Backs White Mesa Dy/Tb Build; Uranium Falls To 10-15% Of Earnings In Five-Year Plan
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: EFTS / TSX: EFR) is transforming from uranium producer to rare earth company, with up to US$725 million in conditional US government support to expand rare earth separation at the White Mesa Mill in Utah and build downstream dysprosium and terbium production facilities. Rare earths are targeted to represent approximately 60% of earnings in five years — up from near-zero today — with uranium falling to 10–15%. The company's recent acquisition of Australian Strategic Materials (ASM) gives it a commercial metal production facility in Ochang, South Korea; ASM's dysprosium oxide passed purity benchmarks at a major Korean permanent magnet manufacturer in December 2025, validating the product. Commercial-scale Dy/Tb production is planned for H2 2026 — a milestone that would make Energy Fuels one of the world's only non-Chinese producers of these defense-critical magnet metals, arriving just weeks before China's November 10 rare earth export control review deadline.

headline: GUNNISON COPPER SCALES TO 6 DRILL RIGS, HUNTS US GOVERNMENT CO-FUNDING — Arizona ISR Project Seeks EDFP Loans That Could Accelerate First Production By Two Years
snippet: Gunnison Copper Corp. (TSX: GCU / OTCQB: GCUMF) expanded from two to six active drill rigs at its Johnson Camp ISR copper project in Arizona in September 2026 as CEO Craig Hallworth confirmed pursuit of co-funding through the US Energy Dominance Financing Program and other government mechanisms including its Defense Industrial Base Consortium membership. Hallworth stated that 50% government co-funding of remaining pre-production capital could advance the timeline by approximately two years. Gunnison's in-situ recovery process requires no open pit, no blasting, and minimal surface disturbance — a profile that aligns with the current administration's permitting priorities for domestic critical minerals. The company already holds $167 million in non-dilutive funding from Nuton LLC and $13.9 million in DOE tax credits; a government loan facility would be additive to both.

headline: T2 METALS HITS 10 g/t AU IN SOIL AT AURORA YUKON — 3,000-Sample Grid Defines Two High-Grade Gold-Copper Targets In Tombstone Gold Belt
snippet: T2 Metals Corp. (TSX-V: TWO) reported September 2 soil and auger sample results from a 3,000-sample grid across its 76 km² Aurora Gold-Silver Project in Yukon's Tombstone Gold Belt, with 1,619 results including anomalies up to 10 g/t gold, 86 g/t silver, and 0.74% copper alongside elevated arsenic pathfinder signatures. The program identified two untested high-grade gold-copper targets ready for drill testing. Aurora was acquired from legendary prospector Shawn Ryan — who has a track record of district-scale discoveries that attracted major M&A attention — and sits in the historic Dawson Mining District where geological work has identified multiple orogenic gold systems predating any placer enrichment. Soil sampling at this scale and density is typically the final pre-drill step; a drill program announcement is likely the next catalyst.

headline: GOLD STOCKS STILL UNDERVALUED AT $4,300 GOLD — GoldSeek: GDX Top-25 P/Es Hit Decade Lows; Autumn Rally Has Substantial Room To Run Before Year-End Correction
snippet: Adam Hamilton's latest GoldSeek analysis argues that gold mining stocks remain significantly undervalued relative to earnings power even after a strong 2026 upleg, with the GDX top-25 average trailing-twelve-month P/E at its lowest level in at least a decade despite gold sustaining above $4,000/oz. Many major producers now trade at low-teens or single-digit earnings multiples — valuations more typical of mature industrials than a sector generating record cash flows. Hamilton identifies the gap between earnings growth and price re-rating as the central opportunity: as retail and institutional investors discover that gold miners are generating cash at a pace that exceeds most sectors in the S&P 500, re-rating pressure is likely to be sustained and potentially abrupt. For junior mining investors, the analysis is a reminder that the carry-through from producer profitability to junior exploration funding is intact and building.

headline: SOLITARIO GOLDEN CREST PHASE 1 DISAPPOINTS — No High-Grade Feeders In First 3 Holes; 0.02-0.40 g/t Au In Ponderosa Limestones; 7 More Holes In Lab
snippet: Solitario Resources Corp. (TSX: SLR / NASDAQ: XPL) reported September 2 that the first three assayed holes from its Phase 1 Ponderosa drilling program at the Golden Crest gold project in South Dakota returned low-grade results: holes PD-001, PD-002, and PD-007 intersected only 0.02 to 0.40 g/t gold in Paleozoic limestones with no high-grade feeder structures identified; the best individual interval was 1.3 metres at 1.37 g/t Au from Precambrian rock in PD-007. Seven additional holes from the 10-hole, 2,949-metre program remain in the laboratory with results expected in late September or October. The release illustrates the inherent uncertainty of early-stage district drilling: the original thesis — that bonanza-grade feeders pass through the Ponderosa target zone — remains untested by these three holes, and seven results still to come will determine whether Phase 1 was a near-miss or a genuine negative.
